objectives.summary: The Colorkeys project aims to enhance music education for children by providing an engaging, color-based method for learning piano and reading music. The project includes a software program that allows children to learn at their own pace, with instant feedback and rewards, and is designed to support school music education. Additionally, for every 100 games sold, a Colorkeys school program package will be donated to a school in need.
key_points: The project aims to make music education accessible to children everywhere at an affordable cost.
Colorkeys is developing a music-based video game to help children learn how to play, read, and enjoy music.
The software levels will be sequential, requiring students to master a concept before moving ahead.
The program allows kids to learn at their own pace and provides instant feedback and rewards to promote learning.
For every 100 games sold, a Colorkeys school program package will be donated to a school in need.
The game will require children to complete tasks and stages before advancing to more material.

It incorporates instructional videos, drag-and-drop activities, and quizzes to reinforce concepts, allowing children to learn at their own pace with instant feedback.

innovation.summary: The Colorkeys project introduces an innovative color-coded note system that enhances music learning for children. This patented approach allows kids to quickly associate musical notes with corresponding keys on a keyboard, significantly reducing the time required to learn music concepts.
key_points: Colorkeys is based on a patented color-coded note system.
The system helps children quickly connect notes on the page with the keys on the keyboard.
Using the Colorkeys method, children can learn in a few hours what typically takes months.
The video game component is designed to be engaging while adhering to sound academic principles.
A point system in the game encourages children to complete activities and play accurately.
Children practice music concepts while mastering songs and understanding theoretical material.
